title: Daily Market Digest - October 17, 2026
subtitle: Review of Friday, October 16, 2026, Trading Session

items.headline: Tech Sell-off Drags Major Indices Lower, Nasdaq Posts Worst Week Since June
items.summary: U.S. equities closed lower on Friday, October 16, 2026, as a broad sell-off in big technology and semiconductor companies weighed heavily on the market, capping the worst week for the Nasdaq Composite and S&P 500 since June. Investor concerns deepened over the sustainability of the AI buildout amid rising borrowing costs and mounting debt, leading to a notable sector rotation. The Dow Jones Industrial Average, however, outperformed, suggesting a shift in investor focus away from highly valued tech. Meanwhile, escalating geopolitical tensions pushed crude oil prices higher, adding to inflation concerns. Not financial advice.

items.headline: Micron Technology

items.headline: Intel Corp.

items.headline: Tech Sector Leads Market Downturn Amid AI Debt Concerns
items.summary: A broad sell-off in technology companies, particularly chipmakers, pulled Wall Street lower. Concerns over higher interest rates and mounting debt-funded AI infrastructure expansion weighed heavily on investor sentiment. The Nasdaq, heavily weighted with tech stocks, saw its worst week since June.

items.headline: Inflation Surpasses Expectations, Fiscal Deficit Widens
items.summary: September's Consumer Price Index (CPI) rose to 3.7% annually, exceeding expectations, with gasoline prices being a significant contributor. The U.S. fiscal deficit for fiscal year 2026 widened to $1.99 trillion, the highest since 2021, driven by record spending and rising debt servicing costs.

items.headline: Energy Sector Outperforms as Oil Prices Surge
items.summary: The energy sector bucked the market's negative trend, with crude oil prices (Brent crude) approaching $110 per barrel. This surge was attributed to escalating attacks in the Strait of Hormuz, adding another layer of inflation concerns.

items.headline: Mixed Q3 Earnings Reports for Major Financials and Tech
items.summary: Key companies reported Q3 2026 earnings. Travelers ($TRV), Truist Financial ($TFC), M&T Bank ($MTB), Citizens Financial Group ($CFG), and Regions Financial ($RF) beat EPS estimates. However, JPMorgan Chase ($JPM) missed, and tech giants like ASML ($ASML) and Taiwan Semiconductor ($TSM) saw declines despite strong AI demand, as revenue misses and weaker margins overshadowed results.
